item.title: China's swimming prodigy Yu clinches first major title from Asian Games
item.description:
Published: 2026-09-20
Gold medalist Yu Zidi (C) of China, silver medalist Chang Mohan (L) of China and bronze medalist Okuzono Misa of Japan pose during the awarding ceremony for the women's 200m butterfly at the 20th Asian Games Aichi-Nagoya 2026 in Tokyo, Japan, Sept. 20, 2026. (Xinhua/Wu Zhizun) TOKYO, Sept. 20 (Xinhua) -- 13-year-old Chinese swimmer Yu Zidi made a sound Asian Games debut on Sunday to secure her first title from major events, as China claimed six gold, one silver and two bronze medals on the opening day of swimming competition at the Games. Yu dominated the women's 200m butterfly in two minutes and 5.08 seconds, setting a new Games record. Fellow Chinese Chang Mohan took silver in 2:08.44. "I hope I can swim even faster," Yu said with a smile. "I believe I will perform better next time." The teenager said she still had room for improvement, particularly in her technique. "I need to lower my head earlier and improve the movement of my legs," she said. For Yu, the gold marked the beginning of her Asian Games journey. She became the youngest swimming world championships medalist in history last year at the age of 12, when she helped China win bronze in the women's 4x200m freestyle relay in Singapore. She is also one of the youngest athletes to be nominated for the Laureus World Sports Awards. China also won the women's 4x100m freestyle relay in a Games record time of 3:33.10. Zhang Yufei said she was "very happy" with the result and felt she had produced a peak-level performance in her leg. Returning to the Tokyo Aquatics Centre, where she had competed at the Tokyo Olympic Games, Zhang said she felt a rare sense of familiarity and comfort. "I really enjoyed it and felt completely immersed," she said. Tang Qianting defended her women's 50m breaststroke title in 29.45 seconds, improving the Games record she set in the morning. "I think I can still do better," Tang said, setting her sights on breaking the 29-second barrier. Olympic champion Pan Zhanle also defended his men's 100m freestyle title in 47.61 seconds. Although the result fell short of his expectations, Pan said he had regained some confidence after a difficult period. "I don't care as much about winning or losing as I used to. I just want to enjoy the competition and leave no regrets," he said. The opening day also saw Xu Jiayu successfully defend his men's 100m backstroke title in an event record of 51.98 seconds, while Li Bingjie retained her women's 1,500m freestyle title in 15:53.52. In the men's 200m individual medley, five-time Asian Games veteran Wang Shun took bronze as Japan's Tomoyuki Matsushita won gold. For Wang, returning to the Tokyo venue brought back memories of his winning Olympic competition five years ago. "It felt like I was making up for the regret of having no spectators five years ago," Wang said. "I really enjoyed it and was completely immersed in it." For Yu, the first day of competition marked the beginning of what promises to be a busy Asian Games campaign, with two more individual events still to come. ■ Yu Zidi of China competes during the women's 200m butterfly final at the 20th Asian Games Aichi-Nagoya 2026 in Tokyo, Japan, Sept. 20, 2026. item.title: China launches new group of satellites
item.description:

A Lijian-1 Y18 carrier rocket carrying nine satellites blasts off from the Dongfeng commercial space innovation pilot zone in northwest China, Sept. 20, 2026. China successfully launched nine satellites into space from the Dongfeng commercial space innovation pilot zone in northwest China at 12:03 p.m. Sunday (Beijing Time). The satellites were carried by a Lijian-1 Y18 carrier rocket and have entered their planned orbits. The launch mission was a complete success. (Photo by Wang Jiangbo/Xinhua) JIUQUAN, Sept. 20 (Xinhua) -- China successfully launched nine satellites into space from the Dongfeng commercial space innovation pilot zone in northwest China at 12:03 p.m. Sunday (Beijing Time). The satellites were carried by a Lijian-1 Y18 carrier rocket and have entered their planned orbits. They will mainly be used for space environment monitoring, disaster prevention and mitigation and scientific experiments. The launch mission was a complete success. This was the 17th flight mission conducted by the Lijian carrier rocket series, which were developed by commercial spaceflight company CAS Space. The Lijian series have so far successfully sent one spacecraft and 121 satellites into space, with a total payload mass in orbit exceeding 21 tonnes, according to the company. The launch schedule for Lijian-1 carrier rocket has been set through the second half of 2027. CAS Space is China's commercial space company that has launched the largest number of satellites and the heaviest payloads in the country's private space sector, the Science and Technology Daily reported Sunday. ■ A Lijian-1 Y18 carrier rocket carrying nine satellites blasts off from the Dongfeng commercial space innovation pilot zone in northwest China, Sept. 20, 2026. item.title: China's new-generation synchrotron radiation facility achieves first beam
item.description:
Published: 2026-09-20
HEFEI, Sept. 20 (Xinhua) -- The linear accelerator of the Hefei Advanced Light Facility (HALF) successfully generated and delivered an electron beam on Sunday, marking a key step forward in the construction of the world's most advanced fourth-generation synchrotron radiation facility in the low-energy range. Located in Hefei, capital city of east China's Anhui Province, the institution is a fourth-generation synchrotron radiation facility operating at a designed energy of 2.2 gigaelectronvolts (GeV) and based on diffraction-limited storage ring technology. It is also a major national science and technology infrastructure project in China. By generating highly intense and coherent light, the facility will serve as a "super microscope" for scientists to probe the microscopic structure of matter. Compared with third-generation synchrotron radiation sources, HALF is expected to produce soft X-rays with more than 100 times higher brightness and coherence. It will enable the development of experimental techniques with greater precision and sensitivity in the spatial, temporal and energy domains, providing an important research platform for studying microscopic particle behavior, the structure of light elements, and changes in the electronic, chemical and spin states of materials. "Successful beam generation and delivery means that we have taken a key step toward the ultimate goal. The electron beam produced by the linear accelerator is the source of synchrotron radiation. Its beam quality, stability and reliability directly affect the performance of the storage ring and the downstream beamlines and experiments," said He Zhigang, chief engineer of the injector system. The project will next enter a critical stage of commissioning, during which the electron beam will be injected into the storage ring. The facility will gradually move toward full-system commissioning and stable operation, He said. Once completed, HALF will become an internationally advanced fourth-generation synchrotron radiation facility in the low-energy range and complement existing synchrotron radiation sources in China by covering a different energy range. It is expected to provide an experimental platform for cutting-edge research in materials science, life sciences and energy science, and contribute to research in areas including high-temperature superconductivity, new energy batteries, aerospace, biomedicine and advanced materials. According to He, once completed, HALF will be open to scientists from both China and abroad, providing a shared research platform for advanced studies in fields such as quantum information, energy, environment and life sciences. ■

item.title: China-Africa cooperation in vocational education builds skills, opens opportunities
item.description:
Published: 2026-09-20
* The skills that carried African competitors to skills competitions like the World Vocational College Skills Competition are among the everyday subjects in classrooms that China and Africa run together. For some, success in competition has opened the door to employment. * Young Africans across the continent are gaining practical skills as China-Africa cooperation in vocational education continues to grow. For many, mastering a skill is ultimately about finding a job, or even starting a business. The longer game is not training one class of students, but enabling African schools to train their own. by Liu Jie and Lin Jing WINDHOEK, Sept. 20 (Xinhua) -- In a workshop in Ongwediva, northern Namibia, fabric rustles as Wilhemina Amadhila measures, cuts and stitches. "Each stitch comes together to form a stunning outfit," said the 22-year-old woman who will take the craft to the 48th WorldSkills Competition to be held on Sept. 22-27 in Shanghai, China. Amadhila and 16 other young Namibians will compete in different categories of the competition. Besides Namibia, other African countries such as Kenya, Egypt, South Africa and Morocco are also taking part in the contest to showcase their technical and vocational skills. This is not the first time African competitors have taken part in skills competitions in China. Their active participation offers a glimpse of growing China-Africa cooperation in vocational education, which has helped endow many Africans with practical skills and opportunities. LEARNING THROUGH PRACTICE At the 2025 World Vocational College Skills Competition held in north China's Tianjin, Angolan student Massak Ventura Noquena Eduardo took silver on the strength of industrial robotics and automated production-line skills learned from Chinese teachers. "I hope to apply what I have learned to Angola's industrialization," he said. The skills that carried him to the podium are among the everyday subjects in classrooms that China and Africa run together. At the Angola-China Institute of Technology, students study mechatronics, industrial robotics and automation. Guo Xiaoyu, a teacher from Baotou Vocational and Technical College in north China's Inner Mongolia Autonomous Region, remembers students who were at first hesitant to even use a multimeter or an oscilloscope. "Vocational education cannot be based on theory alone. Students have to do things with their own hands," Guo said. After a semester of practice in circuit assembly and fault diagnosis, more than 90 percent of them met the required standard. At Ethiopia's Holeta Polytechnic College, Chinese instructor Ma Yujie demonstrated surgical suturing as animal science students gathered around the table, taking turns practicing on training pads. "We are now participating in practical demonstrations," Lemi Abera, 22, said. "With our Chinese instructors linking classroom concepts to practical animal health practices." Ma is one of 20 Chinese teachers working at six vocational colleges across Ethiopia. "The students really cherish the opportunities to practice on training models, to the extent that some are willing to spend extra time in the laboratory after class," she said. In Cameroon, the classroom has moved onto the construction site. In early August, China First Highway Engineering Co., Ltd. teamed up with Cameroon's Ministry of Higher Education and the National Advanced School of Public Works to run the country's first certification course for surveyors. Cameroon's Minister of Higher Education Jacques Fame Ndongo said the program turns construction sites into "open-air classrooms" and builds a direct bridge between universities and major projects. This cooperation is not just about building roads; it is about training people, and about the future of Cameroon's workforce, the minister added. According to an action plan released at the 2024 Beijing Summit of the Forum on China-Africa Cooperation, China will continue vocational education with Africa, build with African countries schools of engineering technology, set up or upgrade 10 Luban Workshops, and offer 60,000 training opportunities aimed chiefly at African women and youth. China has established 17 Luban Workshops in 15 African countries and trained tens of thousands of professionals. FROM SKILLS TO LIVELIHOODS For many young Africans, mastering a skill is ultimately about finding a job, or even starting a business. At the end of 2025, 30 Rwandan students came home from a year of advanced training at Jinhua University of Vocational Technology in east China's Zhejiang Province. Aimable Tuyishime, a 23-year-old e-commerce graduate who studied logistics, warehouse management and data analysis there, is now building an online shopping platform for Rwandan consumers. "This is the right time to put all the skills and experience I gained into practice," he said. In Tanzania, the Kilimanjaro Institute of Technology and Management launched a Chinese culinary program early this year, combining video lessons from chefs in China with practice in local kitchens. "These are skills that make you different, and I can even start my own restaurant one day," said hospitality student Ruth Washima Seni. For some, success in competition has opened the door to employment. At last year's Namibian national skills contest, the gold medalists in cooking and restaurant service also won three-month apprenticeships with a local hospitality group. SEEDS THAT STAY The longer game is not training one class of students, but enabling African schools to train their own. In Cote d'Ivoire, seven modern vocational schools built by Chinese contractors opened last September. Spanning some 83,000 square meters, they can take about 5,600 students in 15 trades, from machining to auto repair and agro-processing. Moreover, 184 Ivorian teachers and administrators from the schools spent four months in China learning to use and maintain equipment, while 15 school managers studied school management there. Two Chinese vocational institutions now help operate five of the schools. In Kenya, China-supported vocational education cooperation is entering a new phase: 69 institutions will receive equipment for 70 training workshops, and 1,190 instructors and technicians will be trained in both countries. "A trained instructor can train many generations of trainees; (and) a modern workshop can continuously produce skilled workers," said Esther Thaara Muoria, principal secretary of the State Department for Technical and Vocational Education and Training in Kenya's Ministry of Education. Wu Jiashun, who heads the central Africa regional center of China First Highway Engineering, put it more plainly: a young person trained today will work for 30 years, and will bring up more young people along the way. "That is how a country learns to build its own roads." For Amadhila and her teammates, Shanghai will be more than a place to compete. It will serve as a global classroom where they can test their skills, learn from their peers and bring new ideas home. Behind these young Africans are more classrooms like these, where young people across the continent are gaining practical skills as China-Africa cooperation in vocational education continues to grow.■

item.title: New river-to-sea canal to boost China-ASEAN trade
item.description:
Published: 2026-09-20
NANNING, Sept. 20 (Xinhua) -- At the ongoing 23rd China-ASEAN Expo, a QR code has become an unexpected star attraction. Visitors scan it to access a virtual reality tour of the newly opened Pinglu Canal, a new trade corridor that is expected to boost economic ties between China and ASEAN. The 134.2-kilometer canal, opened to navigation on Wednesday, is the first river-to-sea canal project planned and coordinated at the national level since the founding of the People's Republic of China in 1949. Running from Hengzhou in south China's Guangxi Zhuang Autonomous Region to the Beibu Gulf, it gives China's landlocked southwest a shortcut to the coast and overseas markets. The economic logic is straightforward. The canal is expected to reduce overall logistics costs by 18 to 30 percent and save more than 5 billion yuan (about 740.51 million U.S. dollars) in transportation costs each year. China's trade with ASEAN exceeded 1 trillion U.S. dollars for the first time last year. In the first seven months of 2026, total trade between the two sides reached 744.41 billion U.S. dollars, an increase of 24.7 percent year on year, accounting for 21.8 percent of China's total foreign trade during this period. For businesses moving goods between China and ASEAN, China's largest trading partner, even a small reduction in shipping time or cost can translate into significant competitive advantage. "This is a canal of significant historical dimension, meaning that it will not only benefit China alone," said Kao Kim Hourn, secretary-general of ASEAN. "I hope that both ASEAN and China take advantage of this great opportunity to deepen our economic cooperation." Kao added that the canal will cut comprehensive logistics costs for goods moving between China and ASEAN, thereby boosting regional economic competitiveness. For Timor-Leste, attending the expo for the first time as ASEAN's 11th member and an official co-host, the canal represents new opportunities. "The Pinglu Canal will serve as a help to get more products from Timor-Leste to come to market in China," said Elias de Jesus Fatima, director-general of commerce at Timor-Leste's Ministry of Commerce and Industry. "Hopefully one day we can engage more of the private sector in China and Timor-Leste to have a deal in cooperation, especially in trade." Chakra Yodmani, deputy permanent secretary of the Ministry of Commerce in Thailand, echoed the sentiment. "The canal will make it much easier and faster to ship our fresh produce to Southwest China," Yodmani said, noting that time is critical for perishable goods. "The savings will benefit both businesses and consumers," Yodmani added. Beyond the shipping route itself, the canal's green construction, smart operations and modern management are also under the spotlight. Environmental protection was a priority during construction. The canal includes a fish passage more than 480 meters long and a dedicated wildlife crossing for land animals including leopard cats and squirrels. A monitoring system powered by BeiDou navigation, cloud computing and artificial intelligence enables early warning of navigation risks across the entire route. After a field visit to the Pinglu Canal, Vietnamese Ambassador to China Pham Thanh Binh praised the project's rapid progress and its use of advanced technologies and innovative approaches. He said the experience gained in its operation and management is worth drawing on for other countries, including Vietnam, and that the project demonstrates China's technological capabilities and its determination to advance regional connectivity. Experts point out that these practices, from ecological protection to smart shipping, align with ASEAN countries' needs for green development and digital transformation. "The experience gained in the canal's construction and operation provides a new reference for regional water transport infrastructure and connectivity," said Jiang Chenxian, a researcher with the Academy of China-ASEAN International and Regional Studies at Guangxi Minzu University. Now that the canal is open to navigation, the focus is turning to operation and industrial development. Zhang Lei, deputy director of the Institute of Southeast Asian Studies at the Guangxi Academy of Social Sciences, noted that the focus will shift to how to make good use of the canal, particularly whether operational factors can deliver stable advantages and translate into tangible, sustainable gains for businesses. Local authorities have rolled out supporting policies covering cargo sourcing and vessel access standards. The new artery carries particular significance for China's southwest, which has long lagged behind the more prosperous eastern coast and faced higher costs getting goods to seaports. Coal, ore, grain, new-energy materials and auto parts from the region can now take a more direct route to overseas markets. "In the near term, the canal is likely to reshape existing cargo flows," said Meng Shuang, an associate professor at Central University of Finance and Economics. Over time, Meng said, the lower cost of reaching the sea could generate new trade, draw investment inland and reshape industrial development along the canal. The changes are also visible to enterprises. Along the canal, pillar industries, including modern green chemicals, artificial intelligence and next-generation information technology, are accelerating their clustering. A petrochemical industrial park in Guangxi's Qinzhou City has gathered more than 60 green petrochemical producers with annual output value exceeding 100 billion yuan. PetroChina Guangxi Petrochemical Company, located within the park, is closely watching market opportunities arising from the canal's opening. "For enterprises, this means water transport, warehousing and transshipment costs are expected to drop further," said Wu Xiaopeng, an official of the company. "The corridor is changing more than just transportation distance," Wu added. "The combination of corridor advantages and industrial clustering will also create more favorable conditions for the landing of projects." ■

item.title: Asian Games | Day 1: China storms opening day with golds, world record and swimming dominance
item.description:
Published: 2026-09-20
by sportswriter Li Jia NAGOYA, Japan, Sept. 20 (Xinhua) -- China made a strong start to the 2026 Aichi-Nagoya Asian Games on Sunday, claiming its first gold medal in the women's team modern pentathlon and setting a world record in shooting. Chinese swimmers were particularly dominant in the pool, winning six of the seven gold medals on offer and helping China finish the opening day with 11 gold medals. China successfully defended its women's team title in modern pentathlon to claim the delegation's first gold medal at the Asiad. The team event is decided by the combined scores of each team's top three finishers. China topped the women's team standings with 4,318 points, powered by solid performances from Zhang Mingyu, Wu Xiyao and Meng Xin. Zhang and Wu also took silver and bronze, respectively, in the individual event. Later in the day, China's Li Liuchang won gold in the men's individual event. The event marked modern pentathlon's Asian Games debut in its new format, with the obstacle discipline replacing equestrian and offering a preview of the sport's format for the 2028 Los Angeles Olympics. Discussing the challenges she faced during the transition, Zhang said, "I had relatively little time to train for the obstacle event, so I had to put in extra effort. I'm also a little older than some of the other athletes, which can affect my physical condition." "But I want to keep moving forward and working hard to overcome these challenges. I believe they are only temporary, and I will continue to work hard," she added. China could have claimed its first gold earlier in the morning in the men's individual triathlon, but favorite Zhang Xirui had to settle for silver as Japan's Takumi Hojo won the first gold medal of the Games. Zhang's silver was China's best-ever result in the men's individual triathlon at the Asian Games. China continued its strong start in the shooting events, winning the women's 10-meter air rifle team title with a world-record score. In the pool in Tokyo, Chinese swimmers, led by Olympic champions Pan Zhanle and Zhang Yufei, turned in a series of dominant performances on the opening day. 13-year-old Yu Zidi made a winning Asian Games debut in the women's 200-meter butterfly, taking gold in a Games-record 2:05.08 and claiming the first swimming gold medal of the Games. Yu had already gained international attention as the youngest swimmer to win a world championship medal, achieving the feat at the World Aquatics Championships last year at the age of 12. The momentum continued as world record holder Pan Zhanle successfully defended his 100m freestyle title in 47.61 seconds, finishing ahead of South Korea's Kim Young-beom and Hwang Sun-woo, who took silver and bronze, respectively. Veteran backstroke specialist Xu Jiayu retained his 100m backstroke title in 51.98 seconds, while distance specialist Li Bingjie won the women's 1,500m freestyle in 15:53.52. In the sprint events, Tang Qianting successfully defended her women's 50m breaststroke title, clocking 29.45 seconds to lower the Games record of 29.50 she had set just hours earlier. China also won the women's 4x100m freestyle relay, with Yu Yiting, Zhang Yufei, Cheng Yujie and Wu Qingfeng combining to claim another gold medal. The only swimming gold China missed went to Japan in the men's 200m individual medley. Tomoyuki Matsushita edged teammate Yumeki Kojima to win the gold. China's veteran Wang Shun took bronze. China's success continued on the wushu court, where Tong Xin retained her women's taijiquan and taijijian all-around title. In the men's events, athletes from Macao, China finished first and second in the changquan competition. In table tennis, the tournament's top Chinese players also got their campaigns underway, with Sun Yingsha and Wang Chuqin helping the women's and men's teams advance to the knockout stages as group winners. China had a tougher time in the men's team sports, with the football team playing to a 0-0 draw with Iran and the basketball team falling 79-70 to Iran to miss out on the bronze medal. China head coach Guo Shiqiang attributed the basketball team's struggles to fatigue and a lack of experience. "We have many young players who need more experience in big games," Guo said. "The players were very tired in the last two games. We didn't have enough players to rotate, so some had to play heavy minutes and became very tired." South Korea won the men's basketball gold medal, beating Japan 67-57 in the final. China led the medal standings with 11 gold, six silver and three bronze medals, followed by host Japan (6-7-7) in second and South Korea (4-3-7) in third. ■

item.title: China builds national computing network as key pillar of new infrastructure
item.description:
Published: 2026-09-20
BEIJING, Sept. 20 (Xinhua) -- As artificial intelligence (AI) and large-scale data processing reshape the global tech landscape, China is accelerating the construction of a nationwide computing power network as a cornerstone of the country's future infrastructure. The computing power network has been incorporated into the national "six networks" infrastructure framework as the 15th Five-Year Plan (2026-2030) enters its first year, marking the industry's shift toward high-quality development, said Wang Jinping, president of the China Association of Information, at an industry conference. The Computing Power Network Industry Conference and AI Computational Power Industry Expo 2026, which concluded recently in Beijing, brought together academicians, researchers, industry leaders and other key stakeholders to explore pathways for building an integrated national computing power network, advancing technological innovation and fostering ecosystem collaboration. Formalized by a top-level decision in April 2026, the computing power network -- alongside the networks of water, next-generation power grids, next-generation telecommunications, underground urban pipelines and logistics -- has become as indispensable to the digital age as water and electricity. It is expected to unlock a new wave of strategic development opportunities. RAPID EXPANSION AND NATIONAL LAYOUT Strong policy support and robust market demand are already propelling China's computing power industry into a new stage of high-quality, large-scale development. As of June 2026, the country's intelligent computing capacity reached 2,185 EFLOPS -- each unit representing 1 quintillion floating-point operations per second -- up 177 percent year over year. More than 70 computing power transmission corridors linking major computing hubs and key regions have been built, and 17 national computing interconnection regional nodes have been approved. Building on this momentum, China is now accelerating the construction of an integrated national computing power network, forming an "8+10+3" spatial layout centered on eight national computing hubs, 10 national computing clusters and three computing-electricity coordination zones. To centrally pool the nation's computing resources, a national computing service platform is accelerating its expansion, steadily connecting platforms across 31 provincial-level regions. Its marketplace has attracted more than 10,000 enterprise users, over 200 service providers, more than 2,000 computing products and over 300 large models, while offering developers computing access services and accumulating billions of monitoring data records. COMPUTING-ELECTRICITY COORDINATION Beyond interconnecting existing facilities, the computing power network is matching supply in resource-rich regions with surging demand in the fast-growing east through "computing-electricity coordination." Regions such as Inner Mongolia Autonomous Region and Xinjiang Uygur Autonomous Region are converting abundant wind and solar power into on-site computing capacity, supporting the east's growing needs for large-scale data processing and AI training. Inner Mongolia offers a telling example. With green electricity priced at around 0.35 yuan (about 5 U.S. cents) per kilowatt-hour, a cool climate that allows natural cooling for nearly 10 months a year and network latency of no more than 5 milliseconds to Beijing, the region has emerged as a preferred destination for large-scale computing projects. As of the first half of 2026, 20 of China's 30 leading private computing companies had established a presence in Inner Mongolia, with combined investment exceeding 200 billion yuan, and nine of the country's top 10 computing service providers had set up operations in the region. GLOBAL REACH AND SERVICE INNOVATION The network's benefits are also extending beyond China's borders. As of early August, Chinese large models had ranked first in call volume for 15 consecutive weeks on model aggregation platforms that mainly serve overseas users, according to data from OpenRouter. More overseas developers are choosing to train AI models in China or directly tap its mature computing resources. Meanwhile, token export services -- providing overseas users with computing and AI services billed by tokens, the basic unit of AI information processing -- have emerged as a new form of services trade at this year's China International Fair for Trade in Services. INTELLIGENT FOUNDATION FOR NEW GROWTH According to Xiao Hongwei, a researcher at the State Information Center under the National Development and Reform Commission, the computing power network, functioning as an "intelligent foundation" for economic and social operations, can not only meet computing demands across diverse scenarios including large model training, film rendering, autonomous driving and smart finance, but also drive upgrades across the entire industrial chain encompassing AI, big data and industrial internet. "The computing power network will fuel the development of new quality productive forces," Xiao said, adding that the six networks are now interwoven and mutually supportive, jointly forming the infrastructure foundation for this new growth paradigm. ■

item.title: China's five-year plan to elevate electronic information manufacturing sector
item.description:
Published: 2026-09-20
BEIJING, Sept. 20 (Xinhua) -- As artificial intelligence (AI) plays an increasingly significant role in reshaping the global industrial landscape, China has recently unveiled a plan to advance its electronic information manufacturing sector, a critical foundation for AI development, over the next five years. The development plan for the electronic information manufacturing industry during the 15th Five-Year Plan period (2026-2030), jointly issued by the Ministry of Industry and Information Technology (MIIT) and the National Development and Reform Commission, aims to further consolidate the pillar role of the industry by 2030. Industrial firms in the sector with an annual main business revenue of at least 20 million yuan (about 2.96 million U.S. dollars) are expected to see their combined revenue surpass 30 trillion yuan, and R&D investment intensity of the sector will rise to 3.5 percent, according to the plan. TO ENHANCE INDUSTRIAL BASE The electronic information manufacturing industry is a major force in the new industrialization drive. By the end of 2025, China's electronic information manufacturing industry had led the country's 41 major industrial sectors in terms of revenue for 13 consecutive years. Building on that foundation, the plan presents a systemic framework to strengthen the industrial base, spanning integrated circuits, electronic components and materials, intelligent sensors, specialized electronic equipment and measuring instruments, and the photonics industry. The framework aims to tackle bottlenecks in key areas and build an independent and controllable industrial base, said Liu Bin, an official with the MIIT. Liu pointed to photonics as an example, noting that advancing breakthroughs in core technologies and establishing pilot testing platforms for key areas and shared needs will strengthen the sector from the ground up. These efforts, he said, will lay a solid foundation for development and accelerate both technological innovation and industrialization process. As a representative sector of the electronic information manufacturing industry, China's integrated circuit industry is entering a new phase of rapid growth, driven by the explosive global demand for high-end computing and memory chips brought about by the AI revolution. Customs data shows that in the first seven months, the country's integrated circuit exports reached 216 billion U.S. dollars, up 99.5 percent year on year, already surpassing the full-year total of 2025. A semiconductor technology company in southwest China's Sichuan Province has already completed its first half-year production targets, and aims to double its output value from last year, according to its general manager. TO STRENGTHEN COMPETITIVENESS While strengthening the industrial base, the plan also sets out strategies to boost the competitiveness of whole devices and systems. This includes enhancing industrial chain resilience in key areas, developing a robust computing ecosystem, and promoting innovation in consumer electronics, among other initiatives. Terminals form the basic foundation of industrial scale and serve as the gateway through which smart technologies reach hundreds of millions of users, said Liang Linjun, a researcher at China Academy of Information and Communications Technology (CAICT). The plan outlines a dedicated push for innovation in key consumer electronics products, ranging from high-end mobile phones and personal computers to virtual reality devices. During the 14th Five-Year Plan period (2021-2025), China's output of core consumer electronics, including mobile phones and computers, maintained a top global ranking. The accelerating evolution of a new generation of AI is bringing new demand, new product forms, and new ways of development to the electronic information manufacturing industry, while raising higher requirements for basic hardware supply and system coordination, said Liang. Liang called for efforts to open up typical application scenarios, develop standards for agent collaboration, high-speed computing interconnect, and hardware-software compatibility, increase long-term capital supply that matches innovation cycles, and train more talent with expertise in both AI and electronics manufacturing. The plan also addresses rising concerns over cutthroat competition in the industry. It calls for timely revisions to industry norms, coordinated planning and early-warning systems for capacity across subsectors, and a comprehensive effort to curb cutthroat competition. As the "hardware foundation" of the digital world, the electronic information manufacturing industry is undergoing profound changes in its strategic position, competitive logic, and growth model, said Ao Li, vice president of the CAICT. Turning scale into systemic strength, as well as moving from leading in volume to winning on quality, will be a major task for China's electronic information manufacturing industry during the 15th Five-Year Plan period, Ao said. Industry insiders say government, industry, academia, research institutions, and users need to work together to translate the plan into results by strengthening the industrial foundation and making the supply chain more resilient. Such a collective push is expected to put China's electronic information manufacturing sector on firmer footing, with a more complete chain and more active innovation, and to lay a solid base for the country's goals of building itself into a manufacturing powerhouse and a cyber powerhouse, they said. ■

item.title: Explainer: How will China's Pinglu Canal chart new economic tides for ASEAN
item.description:
Published: 2026-09-20
HONG KONG, Sept. 20 (Xinhua) -- The Pinglu Canal, China's first national-level river-sea navigation waterway built since 1949, officially opened to traffic Wednesday, marking another milestone in the country's infrastructure development for opening up. Spanning 134.2 km and designed for vessels up to 5,000 tonnes, the canal runs from Hengzhou, a county-level city in south China's Guangxi Zhuang Autonomous Region, to the Beibu Gulf, the closest maritime outlet for much of southwest China. The canal stretches along the New International Land-Sea Trade Corridor, a strategic trade route connecting China's inland regions with ASEAN and other global markets. Functioning as an open regional public good rooted in development-oriented cooperation, the canal underpins the physical conditions for the upgraded China-ASEAN Free Trade Area 3.0 and is expected to reinforce broader regional economic integration in various ways. EASIER MARKET ACCESS TO CHINA The Pinglu Canal cuts the inland shipping distance for southwest-China-bound cargo to the sea by more than 560 km and reduces comprehensive logistics costs by 18-30 percent. The canal delivers a cost-competitive river-sea intermodal shortcut connecting ASEAN producers with the vast consumer market in southwest China. Tropical fruits, aquatic products, grain, rubber, minerals and other bulk commodities from ASEAN can reach Guangxi and China's inland southwest via Beibu Gulf ports and the canal network at lower freight costs and with greater delivery reliability. "The canal becomes the region's shortest and most economical sea-access corridor," Vietnam's Danang News observed in its online report, adding that it will create new impetus for freight transport and trade with ASEAN. For maritime-reliant economies including Singapore, Thailand, Malaysia and Indonesia, the waterway offers an additional viable logistics option for their export-oriented goods, according to Zhang Hongshi, president of the Guangxi Academy of Social Sciences, who added that for land-locked ASEAN member Laos, the canal complements the China-Laos Railway and New International Land-Sea Trade Corridor block trains to expand its connectivity to regional and global markets. Liu Yingkui, researcher at the Academy of China Council for the Promotion of International Trade, noted that ASEAN small-and medium-sized trading enterprises also stand to benefit from new avenues to tap China's inland consumption base. DEEPER CROSS-BORDER INDUSTRIAL COOPERATION Beyond facilitating commodity trade, reduced logistics costs drive shifts in bilateral trade patterns and foster more integrated regional supply chains. ASEAN mineral resources, agricultural produce and seafood can be transported efficiently to southwest China for deep-processing. In return, Chinese manufactured products such as new-energy vehicles, power batteries, photovoltaic equipment and engineering machinery flow to Southeast Asia along the same route, noted Yu Hong, senior research fellow at the East Asian Institute, National University of Singapore. This will boost growth in intermediate-goods trade and closer upstream-downstream industrial collaboration, Yu said. "Large-scale circulation of capital, technology, talent and labor will spur new cross-border investment and industrial-cooperation projects and enable more efficient integration of regional industrial and supply chains," said Lu Xinning, vice chairperson of the regional government of Guangxi. Meanwhile, enhanced connectivity is expected to support the expansion of port-side processing and cross-border logistics services across ASEAN, generating local jobs and enabling fuller participation in RCEP-led labor division, Liu added. CATALYZING INSTITUTIONAL UPGRADES, BROADER OPENING-UP Infrastructure alone cannot automatically deliver full economic dividends, as realising the canal's potential hinges on effective "soft connectivity," Yu said, citing the importance of alignment on customs clearance procedures, mutual recognition of inspection and quarantine results, seamless river-sea intermodal transfer and digital logistics platforms. Yu pointed out that the Pinglu Canal's operational experience in multi-modal transport coordination, standardized vessel specifications and smart customs clearance offers referable practices for ASEAN countries building their own inland-coastal transport systems. Wilson Lee Flores, a columnist for The Philippine Star, believed the canal's significance goes beyond cargo. "Ultimately, infrastructure such as the Pinglu Canal can turn geographic proximity into practical economic opportunity." "If efficiently operated and complemented by good trade policies and sustainable development, it can become an important new link in the ASEAN-China economic relationship, a potential win-win corridor for entrepreneurs, traders, investors, workers, students, farmers, scientists, artists and consumers on both sides," said Flores. Lu said the canal will help build a global hub for opening up. "It will not only greatly elevate China-ASEAN regional cooperation, but also connect China-ASEAN ties with the Belt and Road Initiative by reaching north toward Eurasia, expanding regional opening-up and bringing benefits to ports and transport corridors along its route," Lu said. ■
